newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Verplaetse opposed to EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Verplaetse opposed to EMU delay.

text.p: Belgian central bank governor Alfons Verplaetse was quoted on Tuesday as saying he was opposed to any delay in introducing the euro.

Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer had said on Monday that a delay of European monetary union could be considered if it was clear big countries would fail to meet the Maastricht treaty convergence criteria.
But Verplaetse told Belgian Le Soir newspaper in an interview: "A delay by a day would be like a delay by 10 to 20 years...and that would be a catastrophe for Europe."
"Doing the euro now is a matter of credibility," he said. "If we postpone the euro and start again in 10 years, who is then going to believe we will succeed? It is 'to be, or not to be'."
He said he was certain Germany would meet the EMU criteria and that EMU was not conceivable without Germany and France.
But he added Germany and France would both have more problems than Belgium in reaching their EMU budget target and that Belgium would certainly qualify for the single currency.
"Who could have imagined that for little Belgium," he said.
